get.description: `?assignedToMe=true` is what waits for your decision now (yours, and those of people you stand in for); `?requestedByMe=true` what you asked for; `?decidedByMe=true` what you decided (yourself, or standing in for someone): the history. Filter by `status`, `subject`, `action`, `recordId`, `dueAt`; newest first, cursor pages. Each item has the `can` and the `etag` its `GET /v1/approvals/{id}` would give you (`?fields=` keeps them): decide from the list with `If-Match: <etag>`.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Pages by number instead of cursor: 1 for the first, `limit` rows a page. Example: `page=3&limit=20&count=true`.

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: true: add `total` (counted up to a cap; `totalCapped`).

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description: Conditions in and/or groups, JSON: a condition { field, op, value } or a group { "and": [...] } / { "or": [...] }, 3 groups deep and 30 conditions at most. Example: {"or":[{"field":"assignedToMe","op":"eq","value":…},{…}]}. Fields and operators: assignedToMe (eq); requestedByMe (eq); decidedByMe (eq); status (eq, in, notIn); subject (eq, in); action (eq, in); recordId (eq); requester (eq); dueAt (lt, lte, gte, isNull); createdAt (gt, gte, lt, lte, between); updatedAt (gt, gte, lt, lte, between).

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The order: fields comma-separated, - for descending; the newest first on ties. Example: -dueAt. Sortable: dueAt, createdAt, updatedAt.

parameters.name: fields
parameters.description: Only these fields in each item, comma-separated; id always comes. Example: key,subject. Fields: id, key, subject, recordId, action, status, requester, requesterName, title, link, payload, policyVersion, round, currentStage, stageCount, stageName, dueAt, comment, outcomeReason, endedAt, outcomeAppliedAt, createdAt, updatedAt.

outcomeReason.description: Why it ended without a decision: `overdue`, `not_resubmitted`, `no_approvers`.

outcomeAppliedAt.description: Null until the outcome has been applied (an approved request's effect has run), and again after a resubmission. A banner shows "approved, applying" while `status` is `approved` and this is null.

can.description: What you may do with it now.

etag.description: The ETag `GET /v1/approvals/{id}` would send you now (it covers the request's stages, assignments, timeline and your `can`): send it as `If-Match` on a decision.

nextCursor.description: Pass it as `cursor` for the next page; null: no more (and with `page`).

nextPage.description: With `page`: the next page; null: no more.

total.description: With `count=true`: the rows matching the filters, all pages; the cap when totalCapped.

post.description: No sign-in. The published version its link opens: its name, description and definition, nothing of its tenant.

versionId.description: Send it back with the answers.

format.description: The descriptor format: 1 (fields), 2 (and conditions), 3 (and pages and repeatable groups), 4 (and option sources). Left out: the latest.

visibleWhen.description: Shown only when this holds (format 2): its fields too.

startsPage.description: Starts a new page (format 3): the form is then a wizard, one page at a time.

key.description: The answer's key: unique in the form, and once published its type never changes.

required.description: A checkbox that is required must be checked (a consent).

default.description: Used when the answer is left out: of the field's type.

options.description: The choices of select, multiSelect and radio.

optionsSource.description: In place of `options` (format 4): the choices come from the provider, filtered to what the person filling in may see, and each answer is checked against it on the server. Read them at GET /v1/forms/{id}/options/{key}.

provider.description: A provider registered by trusted server code (GET /v1/forms/option-sources), never a URL or a query.

pattern.description: A regular expression the whole answer must match, in RE2 syntax: no lookaround, no backreferences.

visibleWhen.description: Shown only when this holds (format 2); a hidden field has no answer.

requiredWhen.description: Required, when shown, whenever this holds (format 2).

fields.description: A group's fields (format 3): each item answers them, as an object by key.

404.description: The link is invalid, expired, revoked or used up, or its form is not open (`form_link_not_found`).

post.summary: Open a public form

post.description: No sign-in: the answers to the version the link opened, checked as any submission is (400 with each problem at `answers.<key>`; 409 form_version_outdated when another was published since). Takes one of the link’s `maxSubmissions`. 10 per address in 10 minutes.

parameters.name: X-Captcha-Token
parameters.description: The challenge token (Cloudflare Turnstile, widget action `public-form`), when GET /auth/captcha lists a captcha: always, or once a 403 `captcha_required` asked for one.

parameters.name: X-App-Attestation
parameters.description: A native app's proof instead (APP_ATTESTATION): `ios <challenge> <keyId> <assertion>` (App Attest) or `android <challenge> <token>` (Play Integrity), the challenge from POST /auth/app-attestation/challenge.

400.description: The answers break the form’s rules.

403.description: `captcha_required`: solve the challenge (the problem names `provider`, `siteKey` and `action`) and send its token in `X-Captcha-Token`. `captcha_invalid`: the token was refused (`reason`: `invalid`, `duplicate`, `hostname`, `action`); render the widget again. `attestation_invalid`: the `X-App-Attestation` proof was refused (`reason`). Provider down: 503 `captcha_unavailable` (fail-closed), or 429 `rate_limited` past the fail-open allowance.

404.description: The link does not work (`form_link_not_found`).

info.title: My API
info.description:
Rename and describe your API here (src/core/http/openapi.ts).

Outgoing webhooks are signed with Standard Webhooks (`webhook-id`, `webhook-timestamp`, `webhook-signature`) using the endpoint's `whsec_…` secret, and carry `{ type, timestamp, data }`.

amount.description: The amount in major units, with exactly the currency’s decimals: "12.30", "1200" (JPY), "1.250" (KWD).

subject.description: What it numbers: a permission subject, `Note`.

isDefault.description: What a new record takes when its body names no series and no series' conditions hold for it.

example.description: The number it gives next, if taken now; the fields it prints show as `{field}`.

op.description: Compared as numbers for number fields, as ISO dates for date fields, else as text.

declaredPattern.description: The format in code: used while the subject has no series.

fields.description: The fields a pattern may print (`{title}`; not `boolean` ones), a series take its date from (`date`, `datetime`) or its conditions test.

key.description: What the pattern prints around its counter now; patterns printing the same share the counter.

current.description: The last value taken (0 when none).

next.description: The number the next record gets.

hours.description: The spans worked each weekday, in `timezone`; a weekday with none is closed. A span ends by 24:00 and does not cross midnight: split it over two days.

version.description: Starts at 1; +1 whenever the hours, the zone or the exceptions change. Deadlines already computed keep their value: compare the version they carry.

date.description: A date in the calendar's zone.

hours.description: Special hours that day; left out: closed all day.

calendarVersion.description: The calendar version it was computed with: store it with the deadline.

template.description: One row of the schedule target (`target`), as its schema takes it; checked on create and again at every occurrence, as the owner. The same values are used each time.

rrule.description: An RFC 5545 RRULE, a subset: FREQ (DAILY, WEEKLY, MONTHLY, YEARLY), INTERVAL, BYDAY (weekly: MO,WE), BYMONTHDAY (monthly), and COUNT or UNTIL (20261231). At most 1000 records per schedule. A month without the day (the 31st) has no occurrence.

startDate.description: The first date that may occur, in the schedule's zone.

time.description: Time of day of each occurrence, in the schedule's zone.

occurrences.description: Occurrences handled: created, or skipped after failing for good.

failures.description: Failed attempts at the occurrence due now (3 skip it).

occurrences.description: The next moments records would be created, from now.

enabled.description: False until the tenant turns the rule on.

days.description: The days in force: the tenant’s, else the default.

lastCount.description: Records the last run purged or anonymised.

days.description: The days the count is for.

before.description: Records dated before this are due.

due.description: Records a run would purge or anonymise now.

held.description: Due records a legal hold keeps, which a run leaves alone.

status.description: Only an active rule runs; a change of what it does makes it a draft again.

version.description: Counts the changes of its trigger, condition and actions.

owner.description: `user:<id>` of who activated it: it runs with their permissions.

workers.description: Worker connections: 0 everywhere means no worker process runs.

tenantId.description: The tenant that queued it, when the job names one.

reason.description: Why the last attempt failed: masked as in the logs, cut, no stack trace.

inFlight.description: Being published by this process right now.

lagMs.description: How long the longest-waiting message has waited: the number to alert on.

lastError.description: Masked as in the logs and cut.

state.description: ok: answered now; configured: set up, not probed (run its test); unavailable: did not answer.

driver.description: A name (`smtp`, `s3`), never a URL or a credential.

detail.description: Masked as in the logs and cut.

mail.description: Null for a tenant scope: mail jobs name no tenant.

essential.description: Of them, essential mail: never discarded.

more.description: The limit was reached: call again.

wakeAt.description: When it is next due; null: only a signal or a cancel wakes it.

error.description: Masked as in the logs and cut.

enabled.description: False while DATA_ENCRYPTION_KEYS is not set.

dataKeyId.description: The key new values are encrypted with.

indexKeyId.description: The key new blind indexes are made with.

upToDate.description: No row is on an old key: the old keys may leave the environment.

staleRows.description: Rows, in every tenant, whose value or index is not under the current key.

queued.description: Jobs queued: one per tenant (or the tenantless tables) with stale rows.

hiddenColumns.description: Columns of the view your field permissions hide: left out, not an error.

owner.description: `user:<id>` or `client:<id>`; `anonymous` once its owner’s account is gone.

editable.description: You may change and delete it (its owner, or a template manager).

values.description: Values of the subject's create body (`POST /v1/<path>`), as that route takes them. Only fields it declares and you may set: no ids, numbers, owners or dates the system sets. Required fields may be left out.
The values that still hold: send them (with what the user adds) as the body of the subject's create route, which validates and authorizes them as any create.

dropped.description: Values left out because the schema or your permissions changed since: `unknown` (no longer a create field), `invalid` (the schema refuses it now), `forbidden` (you may not set that field).

dependsOn.description: The fields whose values this one’s choices depend on: ask for its options with `parent.<field>=<value>` for each. When one changes, drop this field’s value and ignore answers still in flight.

fields.description: Parents before the fields that depend on them. Only the fields whose provider you may use.

parents.description: The parent values this answer is for, echoed: show it only while they are still the form’s (an answer for an earlier parent is stale).

value.description: What the form stores and the server checks.

label.description: For display only: never sent back or trusted.

hasMore.description: More match: narrow with `q` (answers hold at most `limit`).

locked.description: An issued document (a generated file): it never changes and cannot be removed; it goes with its record.

scanStatus.description: `pending`: the malware scan has not finished (MALWARE_SCANNER is on) and the file cannot be downloaded yet (409 `attachment_scan_pending`). `clean` otherwise, always when scanning is off. An infected file is rejected: the attachment is deleted and its uploader notified.

renditionStatus.description: Only for JPEG, PNG, WebP and GIF uploads while IMAGE_PROCESSING is on, else null. `pending`: the thumbnail and preview are being made; the original can be downloaded meanwhile. `ready`: `renditions` has them. `failed`: the image could not be processed; the file stays as it was uploaded.

renditions.description: Smaller WebP copies of an image, upright and without metadata: `thumb` fits in 256 × 256 pixels, `preview` in 1600 × 1600. Empty until `renditionStatus` is `ready`. Download one with `GET /v1/attachments/{id}/download?rendition=thumb|preview`.

version.description: The number of the current file: 1, and one more with every replacement or restoration (`GET /v1/attachments/{id}/versions`).

revisionNote.description: The note given with the current version, if any.

versionedAt.description: When the current version was put in place.

current.description: The file the attachment serves now.

note.description: The revision note it was given.

uploadedAt.description: When it became the attachment's file.

lastScan.description: The newest scan (running or not): how fresh the findings are.

total.description: The records to check when it started.

findings.description: Open findings once it completed; null before.

detail.description: `referencedId` (reference), `duplicateOf`: the other records with the same value that you may read, first by id (duplicate), `message` (rule).

FormCondition.description: A predicate { field, op, value } on an earlier field, or { all: [...] }, { any: [...] }, { not: ... }.

data.description: What the texts were made from, and what a client needs to act on it.

link.description: A path of the web app, or null.

key.description: The collapse key, when it has one.

count.description: How many notifications this one stands for (collapsed).

uploadId.description: Send it to `POST …/attachments/complete` once the PUT is done.

url.description: PUT the file here, with the `headers`. Signed for this size and type only, and for ten minutes.

headers.description: Send them as they are (`Content-Type`, and the encryption header when the bucket uses one). `Content-Length` is the file size: the HTTP client sets it.

expiresAt.description: When the URL stops working. The upload may be completed for an hour after it.

maxBytes.description: The largest file, in bytes (ATTACHMENT_MAX_MB × 1024²): larger is a 413 `payload_too_large`.

types.description: The types a file may be (ATTACHMENT_ALLOWED_TYPES), recognized from its bytes: another is a 415 `unsupported_media_type`.

nextPage.description: With `page`: the next page; null: no more.

total.description: With `count=true`: the rows matching the filters, all pages; the cap when totalCapped.

language.description: The language it is written in (`?lang=` of the request).

issuedByName.description: Their name; null when the tenant has no name for them.

finishedAt.description: When it was issued (`completed`) or failed; null while queued or rendering.

error.description: Why it failed, written for people (in the request’s language).

errorCode.description: Why it failed, as a code: `rejected`, `unavailable`…

nextPage.description: With `page`: the next page; null: no more.

total.description: With `count=true`: the rows matching the filters, all pages; the cap when totalCapped.

authorName.description: The author's name, as every member of the tenant sees it; null for anyone the tenant never had.

mentions.description: The people mentioned (`@<email>` or `@user:<id>` in the body) who may read the record, as `user:<id>`.

mentionNames.description: The name of each key in `mentions`: `{ "user:<id>": "Maya Patel" }`. A mention written as an address (`@maya@example.com`) is named under that address too (lower-cased); an address that mentioned nobody has no entry. A person who left the tenant keeps their name; null for anyone the tenant never had.

parentId.description: The top-level comment this one answers; null for a top-level comment.

resolvedAt.description: When its thread was resolved; null if open (always null on a reply).

matched.description: The rules it matched, each the fields whose values are the same (text without case or surrounding spaces).

record.description: The record as you may read it (fields hidden from you left out).

survivor.description: The record as you may read it (fields hidden from you left out).

duplicate.description: The record as you may read it (fields hidden from you left out).

fields.description: The fields you may read on both and change on the survivor: the ones you may choose.

moves.description: The records whose references point at the duplicate and move to the survivor. What other add-ons keep (tags, comments…) follows after the commit.

nextPage.description: With `page`: the next page; null: no more.

total.description: With `count=true`: the rows matching the filters, all pages; the cap when totalCapped.

number.description: 1 for the record's first state, then one more per change.

snapshot.description: The record's changeable fields after the change; fields your permissions don't include are left out.

changes.description: What changed, from → to; null for the first revision.

restoredFrom.description: The revision this change restored; null for an ordinary change.

changedBy.description: Who made the change: `user:<id>` or `client:<id>`; `unknown` for the state a record had before revisions were kept.

changedByName.description: The name of who made the change now; null for `unknown`, system jobs, or anyone the tenant never had.

changes.description: The fields that differ, from `a`’s value to `b`’s.

ai.failed.description: An AI run you asked for failed for good; error is its code.

ai.ready.description: An AI run you asked for finished: read the answer at GET /v1/ai/runs/{id}.

approval.applied.description: An approved request's outcome was applied: outcomeAppliedAt is now set on GET /v1/approvals/{id}.

approval.assigned.description: An approval request waits for you (or for someone you stand in for): GET /v1/approvals/{id}.

approval.decided.description: A decision on a request you made or decide, or its end: status is the request's after it; decision is null when no person decided (cancelled, expired, failed).

bulk.failed.description: A queued bulk run failed for good; items done stay done. error says why, for people.

bulk.finished.description: A queued bulk operation ended; its item results: GET /v1/bulk/{id}.

bulk.progress.description: A queued bulk run is running: items processed so far, every few items.

data.export-ready.description: An export is ready: url is a signed link to the file.

data.failed.description: An export or import failed for good; error says why, for people. The transfer reads failed at GET /v1/data/transfers/{id} by now.

data.import-finished.description: An import ended: how many rows were imported and how many refused.

data.progress.description: An export or import is running: processed rows so far (an import also imported and failed). Throttled; GET /v1/data/transfers/{id} has the same numbers.

document.failed.description: A document you asked for failed for good; error is its code.

document.ready.description: A document you asked for was issued: download it at GET /v1/documents/{id}/download, or as the record's attachment.

notification.description: A new notification, in the recipient's language.

notification.read.description: A notification was marked read (or unread: readAt null).

notifications.read-all.description: before: what the call passed (null: all of them); updated: how many changed.

notifications.unread-count.description: After each of the above: the badge's number.

record.attachments.changed.description: A file on a record you watch was added, removed, scanned clean or processed (an image's thumbnail and preview): ids only.

record.commented.description: A comment on a record you watch (or one you wrote, for your other tabs) changed: ids only, fetch the thread.

record.presence.description: Someone started or stopped viewing or editing a record you are viewing: ids only, fetch GET /v1/presence/{subject}/{recordId}. Advisory, never a lock.
